items.title: Anthropic's record-breaking IPO
points: Anthropic priced its IPO at $83/share, raising $81-107 billion, making it the biggest IPO in history and a major inflection point for the AI industry.

items.title: OpenAI's Foundation & Microsoft Partnership (Dec 2015 & July 2019)
points: OpenAI founded as a nonprofit in Dec 2015 with Elon Musk and Sam Altman as co-chairs, primarily to prevent Google from reaching AGI (artificial general intelligence—AI systems matching or exceeding human capability across all domains).
In July 2019, OpenAI added a for-profit arm and took $1 billion from Microsoft, a structural shift that enabled scaling but seeded future internal conflicts.

items.title: The Transformer Breakthrough (June 2017)
points: Google Brain published 'Attention Is All You Need,' introducing the transformer architecture (a neural network design using attention mechanisms—methods letting a model focus on the most relevant parts of its input) that underlies all modern large language models.
Google had early access but underutilized the breakthrough; OpenAI recognized its potential and built GPT models on it, turning Google's missed opportunity into competitive advantage.

items.title: ChatGPT's Consumer Explosion (Nov 2022)
points: OpenAI released ChatGPT expecting tens of thousands of users; it reached 1 million users in 5 days and 100 million within 2 months, becoming the fastest-growing application ever.

Anthropic had held back its own chatbot since early 2022 over arms-race fears; a rumor of Anthropic's imminent release paradoxically pushed OpenAI to ship first, triggering the broader generative AI wave.

items.title: Sam Altman Ousted and Reinstated (Nov 2023)
points: OpenAI's board fired Altman citing lack of consistent candor but gave no detailed explanation; he was reinstated within 5 days after near-unanimous employee support and a Microsoft offer to hire him separately.
Microsoft's access to OpenAI models was capped at AGI declaration, motivating Microsoft to hire Mustafa Suleyman and build independent AI capability, fragmenting the former OpenAI-Microsoft duopoly.

items.title: Claude 3.5 Sonnet and the Rise of Agentic AI (June 2024 - Nov 2025)
points: Claude 3.5 Sonnet (June 2024) established Anthropic as the coding leader among AI labs.

Agentic capabilities (AI that can autonomously complete multi-step tasks rather than just respond to single prompts) later unlocked Claude Opus 4.5 (Nov 2025), shifting AI's pricing model from $20-30/seat to hundreds of dollars per user monthly.

items.title: DeepSeek's Market Shock (Jan 2025)
points: Chinese startup DeepSeek released its R1 reasoning model (trained via chain-of-thought inference, which requires the model to show step-by-step reasoning), claiming a $5.5 million training cost—a figure later seen as overstated.
The release sparked a $589 billion single-day market cap loss for Nvidia (a 17% drop), the largest one-day loss for any company ever.

Most Western users first encountered reasoning models through DeepSeek, since OpenAI's o1 had only been in limited preview and paid tiers; the event catalyzed US-vs-China framing of AI competition and changed labs' release strategies away from staged previews.

issues.subject: The 10 Biggest Days in AI History

headlines: Anthropic's $83/share IPO raised $81-107 billion, making it the biggest IPO in history and marking a major inflection point for the AI industry.

The transformer architecture (2017) and ChatGPT's launch (2022) were foundational—the former enabled modern language models, the latter created mainstream AI awareness reaching 1 million users in 5 days.
Sam Altman's firing and reinstatement (Nov 2023) weakened OpenAI's perceived invincibility and triggered Microsoft's strategic shift away from OpenAI dependence.

Claude 3.5 Sonnet (June 2024) established Anthropic as the coding leader, with agentic capabilities later unlocking Claude Opus 4.5 (Nov 2025) and changing AI's financial model from $20-30/seat to hundreds of dollars per user monthly.

DeepSeek's January 2025 release caused Nvidia to lose $589 billion in market cap in one day, exposing Western AI labs' release strategies and shifting geopolitical framing to US-versus-China competition.
